facts_of_case: Petitioner filed for annulment of marriage under Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Respondent claimed fraud and non-cohabitation due to dowry demands.

legal_principles.principle: While determining an application under Order VII Rule 11 CPC, only the averments made in the petition can be considered.
legal_principles.held: It is only the averments made in the petition which can be considered, de-hors the averments and the documents which may have been relied upon by the respondent.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Order VII Rule 11

legal_principles.principle: An application under Order VII Rule 11 CPC can be filed at any stage of trial, but the findings must be confined to the averments made in the petition and the documents so relied upon by the petitioner.
legal_principles.held: An application under Order VII Rule 11 CPC can be filed at any stage of trial, with the only rider being that the findings have to be confined to the averments made in the petition and the documents so relied upon by the petitioner.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Order VII Rule 11

legal_principles.principle: A plaint must be read as a whole to determine whether it contains merely an illusion of cause of action and no clear right to sue is disclosed.
legal_principles.held: There cannot be any compartmentalisation, desertion, segregation and inversion of the language to various paragraphs in the plaint. Further, where such meaningful reading of the plaint makes it clear that it contains merely an illusion of cause of action and no clear right to sue is disclosed, then powers of the court under Order VII Rule 11 should be exercised.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Order VII Rule 11
cited_cases: T. Arivandandam vs. T.V. Satyapal (1977) 4 SCC 467

legal_principles.principle: The basic question to be decided while dealing with an application under Order VII Rule 11, CPC is whether the real cause of action has been set out in the plaint or something purely illusory has been stated with a view to get out of Order VII Rule 11 of the CPC.
legal_principles.held: The Apex Court held that the basic question to be decided while dealing with an application under Order VII Rule 11, CPC is whether the real cause of action has been set out in the plaint or something purely illusory has been stated with a view to get out of Order VII Rule 11 of the CPC.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Order VII Rule 11
cited_cases: ITC Limited vs. Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunal and Anr. (1998) 2 SCC 70
